response.sql: WITH j AS (SELECT u.acctscope, f.feerate - f.rebrate AS net FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON o.recordvault = f.orderslink JOIN users u ON u.userstamp = o.userlink), s AS (SELECT acctscope, AVG(net) AS avg_net_rate, COUNT(*) AS fee_record_count FROM j GROUP BY acctscope) SELECT acctscope, avg_net_rate, fee_record_count, avg_net_rate - AVG(avg_net_rate) OVER () AS diff_from_mean_of_scope_averages FROM s

assumptions.assumption: Inner joins drop fees with no matching order, and orders with no matching user.

The net rate is feerate minus rebrate. Records where either is NULL have a NULL net rate, so they are left out of the average. They are still counted in the number of fee records, which is every matched record.
The comparison value is the unweighted mean of the per-scope averages, taken across the scopes that have a non-null average. The difference is scope average minus that mean.

alternatives.interpretation: The number of fee records counts only records with a non-null net rate, i.e. the records actually used in the average.
alternatives.sql: WITH j AS (SELECT u.acctscope, f.feerate - f.rebrate AS net FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON o.recordvault = f.orderslink JOIN users u ON u.userstamp = o.userlink), s AS (SELECT acctscope, AVG(net) AS avg_net_rate, COUNT(net) AS fee_record_count FROM j GROUP BY acctscope) SELECT acctscope, avg_net_rate, fee_record_count, avg_net_rate - AVG(avg_net_rate) OVER () AS diff_from_mean_of_scope_averages FROM s
